title: Influences, uptown upbringing and the district
summary: Hirsch names Philip Gordon as an influence, says he was an uptown boy, and recalls playing for women at the Stag Hotel in the district.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: All right. What do you consider your more important influences in music, Godfrey?

That's hard to answer. I was influenced by Philip Gordon who was a concert pianist. But I mean, during my early days, I mean, I couldn't, I didn't get, I really didn't get around like a lot of these guys did. I was, I was always an uptown boy. I never was downtown. Those that lived like back of town and things in it, they were in a different environment than we were up in the university section. I mean, we didn't, we didn't really go for that particular environment. And you didn't get the chance. I mean, like they tell me about playing in houses of ill repute and things like that. Well, I mean, it wasn't until we were 18 years old that we knew what they were. and the funny thing about it, when one of the young players just about that age of senility that I found it necessary. Instead of raping some young lady, it was cheaper to spend a dollar or two dollars to go down to the district. And we used to go down there, Louie Macinda, Maya Weinberg, Jake Ansberg, and myself. It was four of us. We were in the same band. Making about five dollars at the most or four dollars or three dollars at the night, we'd go down there at the Stag Hotel. And there was a room down there. It was all mirrors and they had a piano in there. And we used to go in there maybe about two o'clock in the morning when things were quiet and we'd play music for them. And they'd start dancing and we'd dance, they'd dance together and we'd dance with them. And after a half hour or so, we'd all disappear to different rooms for a little sex. And that was, that didn't have any great impression on me except that it was fun. And it was cheaper. It was cheaper than getting involved with some dame and supporting her for the rest of your life when you were about time to have a little fun. And this is a problem with today. I mean, I mean, I think today, I mean, kids get too involved too young and it doesn't last. I think if they could satisfy themselves other than the girl that said, now, honey, I'm pregnant, that's it. But, I never did get involved too much. In fact, believe it or not, I never did play with a colored musician in New Orleans.
